body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**

https://www.pombase.org/gene/SPAC637.11

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

This has 

GO:0006401 | NOT RNA catabolic process

from  https://www.pombase.org/reference/PMID:18304578

The results presented herein indicate that both fission yeast proteins play only a minor role (if at all) in mitochondrial RNA degradation. We assume that the RNA-degrading function was taken over by other enzymes in fission yeast mitochondria, while the former degradosome proteins were recruited to new cellular pathways, for example, RNA processing in fission yeast (as discussed in this article) or mitochondrial DNA replication, apoptosis, or chromatin maintenance in eukaryotes, during evolution.
